source_text: Audio itaque Paulum pronuntiantem, quia: Per unum hominem peccatum intravit in mundum, et per peccatum mors; et ita in omnes homines pertransiit, in quo omnes peccaverunt [n52] . Quod tu, non propter exemplum peccati, sed propter generationem dictum esse confirmas; nosque haereticos vocas, qui id ad exempla referamus; illoque te iuvari aestimas argumento: Profecto si Apostolus imitationem, inquis, intellegi voluisset, non " per unum hominem ", sed per diabolum peccatum intrasse, et per omnes homines pertransisse dixisset. De diabolo quippe scriptum est: " Imitantur autem eum, qui sunt ex parte ipsius " [n53] . Sed ideo " per unum hominem " dixit, a quo generatio utique hominum coepit, ut per generationem doceret isse per omnes originale peccatum [n54] . At ego video Apostolum nihil quod ad infamationem generationis spectaret humanae, nihil quod ad condemnationem innocentiae naturalis, nihil quod ad crimen divini operis, protulisse.
pass_a_gloss: I hear therefore Paul pronouncing, because: Through one human being sin entered into the world, and through sin death; and so it passed through into all human beings, in whom all sinned. Which you confirm was said not on account of an example of sin, but on account of generation; and you call us heretics, who refer it to examples; and you estimate that you are helped by that argument: Surely if the Apostle, you say, had wanted imitation to be understood, he would have said that sin entered not 'through one human being' but through the devil, and passed through all human beings. For of the devil it is written: 'But they imitate him, who are from his party.' But for this reason he said 'through one human being,' from whom the generation of human beings certainly began, that he might teach that original sin went through all by generation. But I see that the Apostle brought forth nothing which would look toward a slander of human generation, nothing toward a condemnation of natural innocence, nothing toward a crime of the divine work.

pass_b_english: I hear Paul declaring: ‘Through one man sin entered the world, and death through sin; and so it passed into all human beings, in whom all sinned’ (Romans 5:12). You maintain that this was said with reference to generation, not to an example of sin. You call us heretics for referring it to examples, and imagine that this argument helps you: ‘Surely,’ you say, ‘if the apostle had meant imitation, he would have said that sin entered through the devil and passed through all human beings, rather than “through one man.” For Scripture says of the devil: “Those who belong to his party imitate him” (Wisdom 2:24; Latin numbering 2:25). But he said “through one man,” from whom the generation of human beings certainly began, precisely to teach that original sin passed through all people by generation’ (Augustine, Marriage and Desire 2.45). But I see that the apostle said nothing intended to slander human generation, condemn natural innocence, or accuse God’s work of crime.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
